Title: Stopped, snubbed police, then floored it: Red BMW X6 driver who fled Bukit Bintang roadblock still at large
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — City police are looking for the driver of a red BMW X6 who sped away from a roadblock in Bukit Bintang here at 3.43am last Friday, in an incident that went viral on social media.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department deputy chief Superintendent Suffian Abdullah said initial investigations showed the driver stopped at the roadblock on Jalan Bukit Bintang but refused to cooperate with officers before accelerating away.
“Checks found the incident did not involve any collision or road accident,” he said in a statement today.
“The driver’s identity has yet to be identified,” he said, adding that the department’s team was actively tracing the driver to assist further investigations.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 21(1) of the Police Act 1967, which deals with police duties to keep order on public roads.
He asked the public and any witnesses to call the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or visit the nearest police station.

Title: Bandar Tun Razak gets RM5.7m PM allocation for facility upgrades, Dr Wan Azizah urges residents to help maintain them
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — A total of RM5.7 million in special allocations from the Prime Minister has been channelled to the Bandar Tun Razak parliamentary constituency to upgrade various public facilities from 2025 to this year.
Bandar Tun Razak MP Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said the facilities upgraded included Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Seri Permaisuri and SK Taman Midah 2 under the MADANI Adopted Schools Programme, aimed at enhancing infrastructure, co-curricular activities and students’ character development, as well as mosques, surau and community halls.
“I just want to remind everyone that once these facilities have been upgraded and look better, we must take care of them as a shared responsibility, not leave it solely to Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL). We are the residents who use them, so we must look after them together,” she said at the launch of the 2026 MADANI Kita Programme for the Bandar Tun Razak parliamentary constituency at Perumahan Awam Seri Kota here today, organised by the Federal Territories Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Information Department.
The programme, organised with the support of the Performance Acceleration Coordination Unit (PACU) and the Bandar Tun Razak MP’s office, also saw the handover of 20 eKasih motorcycles and 300 RAHMAH Baskets containing food and essential items.
Various initiatives and direct services for the public were also offered at the programme, themed “Realising the People’s Hopes”, including Jualan RAHMAH, Jualan Agro MADANI, old helmet exchange, motorcycle engine oil changes and free haircuts.
Wan Azizah said the organisation of such outreach programmes was aimed at ensuring that government policies and plans were genuinely felt by the people, right down to the grassroots level.
“Our theme, ‘Realising the People’s Hopes’, has a clear meaning. The government goes directly to the ground to ensure that policies and plans do not merely look good on paper, but that their benefits reach the people and are felt at the grassroots level.
“The success of this programme is not measured by how many booths are set up, but by how many public matters have been made easier and how many problems we have managed to resolve,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Half the old rate, please: Kedah consumer group’s plea after BN vows to bring back GST
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — A consumer group today urged the next federal government to consider starting the Goods and Services Tax (GST) at just 3 per cent, half the rate charged before it was scrapped in 2018, should the tax return.
Consumers Association of Kedah president Mohamad Yusrizal Yusoff said a lower rate would be more manageable because prices of necessities were already too high compared with people’s incomes.
“If this GST can ease the people’s burden, impose it at a low rate, which is three per cent, as a start,” he was quoted by Berita Harian as saying.
“At the same time, we hope full exemptions will be given on basic necessities and on purchases by low-income groups to ease their burden,” he added, referring to the bottom 40 percentile of income earners categorised as B40.
He was responding to Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi who earlier today pledged to bring back GST if the coalition returns to federal power after the 16th general election.
Yusrizal said rising living costs were squeezing consumers and traders alike, as weaker purchasing power slowed business.
He asserted that the current Sales and Service Tax (SST) is a cascading tax charged at every stage of the supply chain, with 8 per cent passed from manufacturers to wholesalers and then retailers, pushing up final prices step by step.
He said GST, by contrast, lets manufacturers and wholesalers claim back the input tax they pay, which makes the calculation more transparent and fairer.
He said the confusion over GST last time came from a lack of clear explanations for consumers, and from tax being itemised on every receipt, which made people feel more burdened than under SST, where the tax is hidden in the selling price.
He also urged the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry to be more proactive in stopping unreasonable price increases.
“The ministry already has legal provisions through the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011 that can be fully used to curb profiteering, thereby protecting consumers’ rights,” Yusrizal said.
GST was introduced at 6 per cent on April 1, 2015, and replaced by SST on September 1, 2018.

Title: Fadhlina: Values-based education must start in preschool to curb youth social ills
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Values-based education and character building must begin as early as the preschool level to nurture a generation that respects others and demonstrates empathy, says Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said quality education was not merely about teaching children to read, write and count, but also about shaping them into individuals with good values and strong character.
“This effort certainly requires the support of parents, teachers and the community at large. What is taught in school must also be nurtured at home, as children learn not only from what we tell them but also from what they observe in their daily lives,” she said in a Facebook post today.
Fadhlina also expressed her appreciation for the concern and views expressed by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, over increasingly worrying social issues involving the young generation.
“The concern by His Royal Highness serves as a reminder that efforts to shape a child’s character cannot wait until they reach their teenage years,” she said.
On Nov 18, Tuanku Muhriz voiced concern over the rise in social problems among youths, prompting the introduction of the Modul Aulad Sejahtera (Child Well-being Module), an early intervention initiative aimed at shaping character, instilling noble values and strengthening children’s identity from the preschool level.
His Royal Highness said the module was developed in response to worrying social trends, including drug abuse, illegal street racing and other negative behaviours that threaten the future of the young generation.
Meanwhile, Fadhlina said 8,365 preschool pupils under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Negeri Sembilan would benefit from the Modul Aulad Sejahtera, which emphasises the development of good conduct (adab), noble values, emotional well-being and social skills.
She expressed hope that the initiative, introduced in Negeri Sembilan, could serve as a model for nurturing a knowledgeable generation with strong cultural values. — Bernama

Title: ‘Take back Dusun Tua’: DAP gears up to reclaim Selangor seat it handed to Umno in 2023
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 22 — DAP wants Dusun Tua back, with state chairman Ng Sze Han saying the party will contest the seat in the next Selangor election after giving way to Umno in 2023.
He told the party’s Selangor convention here today that DAP had been ready to give way to its unity government partner in the last election, The Star reported.
“In 2018, DAP won in Dusun Tua. In 2023, in the spirit of the unity government, we chose not to contest the seat. However, in the next state election, we will contest and take back Dusun Tua,” the Kinrara assemblyman was quoted as saying.
Ng called on all DAP members in Hulu Langat to get ready from today.
He said Bangi MP Syahredzan Johan and Balakong assemblyman Wayne Ong had been appointed Dusun Tua coordinators, with the election machinery running under their leadership.
DAP’s Edry Faizal Eddy Yusof held Dusun Tua from 2018, but the seat went to Umno’s Johan Abd Aziz in 2023, who won by 3,014 votes under the Pakatan Harapan-Barisan Nasional seat-sharing deal.
Ng also called for more state seats in Selangor, saying the assembly has stayed at 56 seats since 2003 even as the electorate grows.
He said Undi18 and automatic voter registration had added many new voters, and more families were moving to the state.
He pointed to the gap between his own Kinrara seat, with 134,016 voters, and Sungai Air Tawar, with just 20,336.
“As the population grows, the number of elected representatives must grow as well,” he said.
Ng added that Selangor DAP elected representatives would be given special portfolios to strengthen the party’s defence ahead of the next state election.
“DAP must not take electoral support for granted. It must remain humble, work harder and respond to the changing expectations of Selangor voters,” he said.

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim unwell, receiving hospital treatment, son confirms
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 22 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim is reportedly unwell and is currently receiving treatment at a hospital here.
This was confirmed by his son, Naim Ismail, when contacted by Bernama today.
“That is correct, (Ismail) is unwell,” he said briefly via WhatsApp.
Meanwhile, the MB’s press secretary, Mohd Fasha Musthafa, indicated that the condition of Ismail who is also the state assemblyman for Juasseh, is showing signs of improvement.
He also expressed gratitude for the public’s concern and requested that everyone pray for Ismail’s speedy recovery and good health. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan swearing-in falls through, source claims some exco nominees pulled out
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Nov 22 — The swearing-in of Negeri Sembilan’s new state executive councillors, reportedly set for Istana Besar Seri Menanti here today, did not take place, Sinar Harian reported.
Citing an unnamed source, the Malay newspaper said the ceremony was called off after several people linked to the new line-up allegedly pulled out at the last minute.
“Earlier, they held a meeting and were informed that some parties had withdrawn. Therefore, the swearing-in ceremony could not proceed,” the source was quoted as saying.
The Star reported separately that it contacted a Negeri Sembilan assemblyman about the ceremony and was told the matter should be referred to the palace.
Malay Mail was not able to verify the information independently.
Local media reported that seven new exco members were expected to form the state administration, down from 10 previously.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had said the appointments would be made soon after receiving the consent of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Last Friday, 24 of the 25 Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional assemblymen in the state agreed to abide by their leadership’s directives and party decisions to resolve the impasse.
The state has been without an executive council since Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of 10 exco members in September, leaving Ismail to lead the government alone.
BN said Ismail had resigned on November 16, but he denied submitting the letter, and on November 20, Tuanku Muhriz decreed that he stay on as menteri besar.

Title: Books, not TikTok: Fahmi calls for early reading habit among children
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Parents should
encourage their children to read physical books from an early age to build a
strong literacy foundation and prevent them from becoming too absorbed in
social media and digital devices, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi
Fadzil said.
He said without strong reading habits, young
people risk spending more time browsing social media platforms such as TikTok
rather than exploring quality reading materials that are essential for
intellectual development.
“I raise this concern because without a good
reading foundation and a sustained interest in reading, our children may end up
wanting only to spend time on TikTok or lose interest in exploring storybooks.
“Reading books not only builds vocabulary but
also provides us with a much broader experience,” he said at the closing
ceremony of the 2026 Lembah Pantai MYReaders programme here today.
Fahmi said while digital technology had
become an integral part of daily life, reading physical books should not be
sidelined as it remained an important foundation for children’s learning and
personal development.
He noted that several developed countries were
also placing renewed emphasis on conventional reading and writing practices,
including Sweden, where efforts were being made to reduce students’ dependence
on digital devices.
The Lembah Pantai Member of Parliament said
exposure to reading materials in various languages, including English, should
also be strengthened to ensure young people were comfortable communicating in
different languages in the future.
To expand the benefits of the literacy
initiative, Fahmi said he planned to double the allocation for the MYReaders
programme from RM50,000 to RM100,000 next year, in conjunction with its 10th
anniversary.
The additional funding would be used to extend
classes to several new locations across Lembah Pantai, following feedback from
parents who preferred to send their children to classes closer to home.
He also announced RM100 book vouchers for all
54 participants in this year’s programme, which was conducted at three
locations - the Lembah Pantai Work and Training Centre, the Kerinchi
People’s Housing Project (PPR) and Sri Cempaka PPR.
The vouchers are intended to encourage participants to
purchase new reading materials ahead of the upcoming school holidays.
“Use the vouchers to purchase several books in
both Bahasa Melayu and English to help instil a love of reading among
children,” he said.
Earlier, Fahmi said the programme, now in its
ninth year and organised in collaboration with non-governmental organisations
(NGOs) in the constituency, had benefited more than 300 participants.
He said it had helped foster an interest in
reading, improve children’s spoken English proficiency and build their
self-confidence.
Following the encouraging response, Fahmi said
he was targeting a 50 to 100 per cent increase in participants next year,
depending on the number of tutors and volunteers available. — Bernama

Title: Penang survey: State govt scores 70.8pc satisfaction, federal govt 59.6pc
Article:
SEBERANG PERAI, Nov 22 — The Penang Satisfaction Survey 2026 found that 70.8 per cent of respondents were satisfied with the state government’s performance, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today.
He said the Penang Institute surveyed 1,686 people on how well the state government addressed issues and carried out policies and development projects that affected their lives.
“Among the findings, 86 per cent of those aged 15 to 24 were satisfied with the state government, well above the overall average, while the figure for those aged 60 to 74 was 72 per cent,” he said.
He was speaking at a Deepavali open house hosted by Penang DAP and the Perai state constituency at the Taman Chai Leng Multipurpose Hall here today, which drew about 2,000 people from various ethnic backgrounds.
According to him, Indian respondents recorded the highest satisfaction level with the state government at 82 per cent, followed by Malay respondents at 74 per cent and Chinese respondents at 66 per cent.
Chow said the survey found that 59.6 per cent of respondents were satisfied with the federal government, he said.
He said the survey methodology allowed the sample of 1,686 respondents to represent Penang’s population.
“People want to see how government policies affect them, what benefits projects bring and what changes they can see in their daily lives, including in traffic management, flood mitigation, water supply, healthcare and education,” he said.
He said state leaders, elected representatives, local councillors and government agencies should pay attention to differences in satisfaction levels across age and ethnic groups, urging them to keep improving public service.
Chow said he was determined to retain Penang in the next election and that doing so would require sustained effort and cooperation from all involved.
Also present were Penang DAP chairman Steven Sim, state Housing and Environment Committee chairman and Perai assemblyman Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo, Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng and other state DAP leaders. — Bernama

Title: Umno open to GE16 talks with Perikatan to ‘ensure that Umno and BN remain relevant’, says VP Khaled
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Nov 22 — Umno cannot expect to win the 16th General Election on its own, vice-president Datuk Seri Khaled Nordin said today as he signalled the party is ready to negotiate with Perikatan Nasional (PN).
His remarks come a week after Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Barisan Nasional (BN) had no plans to extend its cooperation with PN to the general election.
“Umno knows that going alone is unlikely to bring victory. That is why we will discuss,” Khaled was quoted by the New Straits Times as telling reporters here today.
Khaled, who is also Kota Tinggi MP, was responding to PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, who said negotiations with BN could be difficult, particularly over seat allocation.
Khaled said a shared political goal should come before differences.
“Each party is entitled to its own views, but we believe we have a bigger goal,” he added.
He said BN would use its experience in the state elections in Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka, from seat-sharing to a common manifesto, as a guide for the general election.
BN won 48 of 56 seats in Johor, while the BN-PN partnership in Negeri Sembilan won a combined 25 of 36 seats.
In Melaka, the arrangement – which excluded PN component Bersatu as it ran under its own logo – won 24 of 28 contested in Melaka, giving it a two-thirds majority.
“I am going in with a positive approach. If others go in intending to sabotage it, then it will fail. But we are going in to ensure that Umno and BN remain relevant,” Khaled said.

Title: Anthony Loke: Discuss ‘big tent’ idea in PH Presidential Council, not in the media
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 22 — The “big tent” proposal and other political strategies involving Pakatan Harapan (PH) should first be brought to its Presidential Council for discussion and not aired publicly, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke.
“Everyone has their own views and suggestions, but I believe that if we make suggestions publicly and discuss them through the media, we will not achieve the desired intentions or objectives,” he told reporters after opening the Selangor DAP 2026 Convention here today.
He was commenting on Amanah secretary-general Muhammad Faiz Fadzil’s suggestion that PH adopt a “big tent” approach and embrace more Malay-based parties to boost support among Malay voters ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).
Loke also said DAP was open to the proposal for component parties to use their respective party logos in GE16, but this would require further discussions within PH before a final decision was made.
“What is most important is that we must consolidate our strength and find the best approach to face the election. However, such a proposal must first be discussed at the Presidential Council.
“DAP will give its views, and of course, we have suggestions on how to move forward in the coming election,” he said.
On another matter, Loke said the status of his resignation as Transport Minister on Nov 10 was subject to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s decision.
“As far as I’m concerned, I already resigned,” he said.
On Nov 13, Anwar said the government need not rush into deciding on Loke’s resignation, although the official letter on the matter had been received, adding that it required careful consideration.
On Nov 12, Loke, who is also Seremban MP, reiterated his decision to stand by his resignation with immediate effect following the High Court’s decision to allow former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. — Bernama

Title: Zahid’s aide says plan to relocate Rohingya to Turkiye still on, pending clarification
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Malaysia remains committed to pursuing a proposed relocation of Rohingya refugees to Turkiye under a structured skills training programme, although the initiative remains subject to further clarification and coordination with relevant parties.
Shuhaimi Mohamed, press secretary to Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, said the earlier statement regarding the proposed initiative was issued because efforts were indeed underway, with the ultimate aim of serving the best interests of the country and its people.
He said certain matters still required further clarification and coordination with relevant parties before the proposed arrangement could proceed.
“We remain committed to pursuing this proposed arrangement, and further announcements will be made once the necessary processes have been completed,” he said in his Threads update.
The clarification followed a Facebook post by Ahmad Zahid announcing the proposed initiative that was subsequently taken down which drew public attention to the status of the plan.
Yesterday, Ahmad Zahid said that a total of 10,000 Rohingya refugees from Malaysia would be resettled in Turkiye through a structured skills training programme as part of the government’s strategic effort to address the presence of this ethnic group in the country in a more organised, effective and humane manner.
He said the approach went beyond merely sending Rohingya refugees to a third country, as it offered them the opportunity to build a new life through a Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programme lasting three to six months
Shuhaimi said further updates on the initiative would be provided once the necessary processes had been completed.
“Insya-Allah, we will provide further updates soon,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Police foil underground cable theft but suspects flee after chase from Malim Jaya to Alor Gajah
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 22 — Police foiled an attempt by a group of individuals to steal underground cables in Taman Malim Jaya here yesterday, but the suspects managed to escape after a car chase involving several police patrol vehicles.
Melaka Tengah district police chief ACP Halim Abas said the suspects, travelling in a dark blue Proton S70 and a white Toyota Hilux, fled when police arrived at the scene after receiving information about their activities at 6.05 am.
He said police personnel conducting crime prevention patrols received the information from the Melaka Tengah District Control Centre, prompting a pursuit that began in Taman Malim Jaya and passed through Batu Berendam, Krubong and Cheng before ending in Rumbia, Alor Gajah.
“Checks at the scene found several individuals opening underground utility manhole covers, suspectedly to steal cables, but they fled upon realising the presence of the police.
“The individuals escaped in the two vehicles before managing to evade the police,” he said in a statement today.
Halim said preliminary investigations found that underground utility manhole covers at Jalan Malim Jaya 2/2 and Malim Jaya Roundabout had been opened, but the individuals had failed to cut the cables.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing public servants in the discharge of their duties.
He urged members of the public with information about the incident or who could identify the vehicles involved to contact any nearby police station or the investigating officer to assist in the investigation.
Yesterday, a video recording of a group of individuals suspected of being involved in underground cable theft in Taman Malim Jaya went viral on Facebook after it was uploaded by Allex Seah, the owner of the account, who is also the Kesidang state assemblyman. — Bernama

Title: Oil blending at sea is banned, but who watches the shore tanks? Maritime Network chief calls for closer monitoring
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Malaysia’s ambition to strengthen its position as a regional oil trading and bunkering hub requires effective monitoring of petroleum cargoes, including those transferred, stored and handled at shore-based facilities, said Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan.
Jeyenderan who has raised concerns over the commingling of oil cargoes, said that while international maritime regulations prohibit certain oil-blending activities on board ships during sea voyages, attention must also be given to how petroleum cargoes are handled after they are discharged at ports.
In a statement today, he said oil cargoes may be transferred between storage tanks, combined with other products, processed or re-exported before reaching their final destinations.
Such activities are not automatically unlawful, he said, but must comply with customs and licensing requirements, particularly in relation to cargo documentation and declarations.
Jeyenderan pointed to Regulation 5-2 of Chapter VI of the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), which prohibits the physical blending of bulk liquid cargoes on board ships during a sea voyage.
The regulation was introduced through an amendment adopted by the International Maritime Organization (IMO) in May 2012 and came into force on January 1, 2014. The rule, which remains in force, also bans production processes from being carried out on board.
In practical terms, a tanker cannot use its onboard pumping system to circulate different cargoes during a sea voyage with the intent of producing a new petroleum product.
However, moving cargo between tanks is not in itself prohibited. Neither is combining identical cargoes that do not result in a new product, according to guidance published by Gard, a protection and indemnity (P&I) club.
The regulation also provides exceptions for cargo transfers carried out for the safety of the ship and crew or to protect the marine environment. Ships supporting offshore seabed-mineral operations are also excluded.
Although the term “sea voyage” is not specifically defined in the regulation, the shipping industry generally takes it to mean the period when a vessel is outside port limits, as determined by the respective port authorities.
“At sea the rule is clear, you may not turn a tanker into a refinery. Ashore, the question is not whether the law exists. It does,” said lawyer GK Ganesan.
“Section 35N of the Customs Act 1967 requires those who store and handle goods held for transhipment to keep records of their receipt, handling, storage and delivery. The question is whether those records were kept, and whether they match what was declared.
“If oil goes into a tank as crude and comes out as fuel oil, the paperwork should say so. A declaration describes a cargo. It cannot turn it back into what it was.
“Nobody has said a law was broken, and nobody should assume it. But a transhipment hub runs on trust, and trust runs on records,” said Ganesan.

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB appointment up to Yang di-Pertuan Besar, BN won’t interfere, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is leaving the appointment of the next Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar entirely to the discretion of the state’s Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said he would not act contrary to the provisions of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution.
He said BN and Umno would also not interfere in matters concerning the state’s customs and traditions, including those involving the Dewan Keadilan Undang, leaving such matters to the relevant parties to resolve.
“In my view, the interests of the people must take priority. If there are ongoing issues involving the customs and traditions of the Dewan Keadilan Undang, these are not matters for BN or UMNO to interfere in,” he said.
Speaking to reporters after the MCA Central Delegates general assembly here today, Ahmad Zahid was asked whether Datuk Ismail Lasim would remain as Menteri Besar if he secured the support of a majority of state assemblymen.
Also present were BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir and MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong.
Ahmad Zahid said the priority now was to ensure the Negeri Sembilan government continued to function smoothly, particularly ahead of the state legislative assembly sitting to table the 2027 state budget.
In a related development, Ahmad Zahid cautioned leaders of BN component parties against using the media to air differences in views or positions on issues that could confuse the public.
He said any misunderstandings within the coalition should instead be resolved privately at the highest leadership level of the respective component parties.
“I hope there will be no polemics among leaders of BN component parties. Even if there are misinterpretations or misunderstandings, this is not the time for polemics.
“If there is a misunderstanding over an issue, do not use the media to express our positions. Let the top leadership of the component parties resolve it. We do not want the public to be confused or misinterpret the issue,” he said.
The reminder was seen as referring to recent public statements by component party leaders, including MCA Youth’s proposal to reintroduce local government elections in the Federal Territories, as well as Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan’s remarks on the need to align BN’s political stand at federal and state levels. — Bernama

Title: BN sitting out Sarawak polls good for state’s stability, says Fadillah as GPS eyes another big win
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 22 — Barisan Nasional’s (BN) decision not to contest in the 13th Sarawak State Election is a positive move towards political stability in the state.
Sarawak’s Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) Parliamentary Chief Whip Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, said the decision on whether a party should contest an election or otherwise was entirely its prerogative.
“I would like to express my appreciation as Barisan Nasional (BN) has, from the outset, not contested in Sarawak. I also thank other parties that have decided not to contest.
“Democracy is still alive in Malaysia, but it is up to them whether they want to contest or not,” said the Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) Senior Vice President when speaking to reporters after attending the ‘Juh Kita Melabur, Anak Sarawak’ programme organised by Amanah Saham Nasional Berhad (ASNB) here today.
Besides PBB, GPS comprises Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and Parti Demokratik Progresif (PDP).
Nominations are on Nov 28, with Dec 8 set for early voting and Dec 12 for polling.
In the previous state election in 2021, GPS won 76 of the 82 seats contested. — Bernama

Title: Fadillah: 61pc of Malaysians lack RM1,000 in emergency savings, financial literacy must be strengthened
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 22 — A total of 61 per cent of Malaysians do not have savings of at least RM1,000 for emergencies, according to a 2024 Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) report.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said this meant that a significant proportion of the population did not have sufficient savings to cope with unexpected circumstances.
He said 37 per cent of Malaysians also did not have enough savings to cover three months of expenses in the event of job loss.
“These are among the challenges reflected in the facts and figures presented by Bank Negara Malaysia. Therefore, I believe financial literacy is very important and must continue to be enhanced,” he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the Juh Kita Melabur, Anak Sarawak programme at the Amanah Saham Nasional Berhad (ASNB) Kuching branch here today.
Meanwhile, ASNB chief executive officer Fadzihan Abbas Mohamed Ramlee said financial education should be instilled from a young age to nurture a generation that was more financially savvy.
He said an early understanding of the value of money, the importance of saving and basic investment principles would help young people make better financial decisions as they entered adulthood.
“We also greatly appreciate the response from the Sarawakians to the various financial education programmes organised previously.
“This response shows that there is genuine interest among the people in the state to learn, save and invest,” he said.
Building on the relationship and trust established, Fadzihan said ASNB had introduced the Juh, Melabur Menang Mas Campaign specifically for the Sarawakians.
He said the campaign, which runs from Nov 1 to Dec 31, was open to unit holders who met the eligibility requirements as participants from Sarawak.
Under the campaign, every accumulated net investment of RM5,000 made and maintained until the end of the campaign period would qualify participants for one automatic entry into a lucky draw, subject to the terms and conditions. — Bernama

Title: Flights to Indonesia, Thailand and Brunei: RMAF chief doesn’t rule out meth smuggling abroad
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — The drug smuggling ring that has rocked the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) may have reached beyond Malaysia’s borders, its chief has warned.
General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris said the arrested pilots did not fly only between peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak, but also on missions to Indonesia, Thailand and Brunei, Berita Harian reported today.
“So, I do not rule out the possibility that the drug smuggling extended overseas despite strict baggage screening before departure and upon arrival in the destination country,” he was quoted as saying.
He said gaps in baggage screening and security checks, or the use of personal connections to get around inspections, may have made the smuggling possible.
“These drug trafficking cartels have very large and organised networks. So, we leave it to the police to investigate and dismantle this syndicate,” he told the Malay newspaper.
Muhamad Norazlan added that the RMAF would not tolerate any misconduct.
He said the air force launched a full internal investigation as soon as the case surfaced, including a review of the detained personnel’s backgrounds and disciplinary records, particularly those of the pilot involved.
The RMAF is also supporting the detained pilot’s wife, who may be distressed by his arrest, he said.
He said the personnel who exposed the case would be rewarded “for having the courage to do the right thing, even though it involved their superior officers”.
The RMAF will also safeguard their welfare, as they have now become targets themselves, he added.
Seven RMAF personnel and officers were detained earlier this week after 96.6kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million was found at Subang Air Base, along with six civilians arrested in the Klang Valley, Labuan and Tawau.
Police said preliminary investigations showed the syndicate abused access to military aviation facilities to move drugs across the South China Sea via Sabah, bound for neighbouring countries including Indonesia and the Philippines.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said earlier that a routine check of luggage due to be loaded onto an RMAF aircraft at the base led to the discovery of five bags and a box of drugs.

Title: ‘Deal is still on’: Tuition platform keeps its RM200,000 promise to Muar even after Syed Saddiq misses Ironman target
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman may have missed his 12-hour Ironman target, but children in Muar will still get the RM200,000 worth of free tuition promised to them.
Tuition platform PTTI said in a social media post that it would honour its pledge because the Muar MP had not let it down.
“The ‘deal’ is still ‘on’,” it said.
PTTI said Syed Saddiq had given everything he had on one of the toughest Ironman courses in the world, which was the spirit it wanted to support.
He finished Ironman Malaysia in Langkawi yesterday in 12 hours, 48 minutes and 38 seconds, missing the sub-12-hour mark needed to unlock the pledge.
He cramped several times over the final 20km of the course.
After crossing the finish line, the former youth and sports minister apologised to Muar residents for failing to finish within 12 hours, Harian Metro reported.
He said he did his best but nearly gave up in the heat, with his watch showing 36°C, and that strong winds made the race even tougher.
He added that he vomited and suffered repeated cramps near the finish, and that he was happy to have completed the race but torn because he could not make Muar residents happy.
Last year, he finished in 12 hours, 22 minutes and 18 seconds, beating a 13-hour target and earning a RM1 million donation from fashion company Prima Valet for Muar residents.

Title: BN will reinstate GST ‘immediately’ if it returns to Putrajaya in GE16, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Malaysia could see the return of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) if Barisan Nasional (BN) retakes Putrajaya in the next general election.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said GST was a fairer and more targeted system than the Sales and Service Tax (SST) now in place, the New Straits Times reported today.
“I am determined, together with my colleagues in BN, that if we return to Putrajaya, we will immediately reinstate GST,” he was quoted as saying in his speech at the 4th General Assembly of the 30th MCA Central Delegates here.
According to Zahid, “more than 170 countries have implemented GST, while Malaysia is still implementing SST”.
He added that BN is looking back at the past and credited former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, whom he called “Bossku”, for doing his best at the time.
Drawing on his eight years as BN chairman, Zahid also urged all component parties to set aside their differences and close ranks.
He said there were times when the coalition’s unity was nearly fractured, with certain quarters trying to undermine ties between component parties and disagreements straining relations.
“Enough is enough. If we truly want to win the next general election, we must put an end to this habit of finding fault with one another,” he said.
Quoting a Chinese proverb about seeking common ground while respecting differences, he said it should be a guiding principle for cooperation within BN.
He said the founding leaders of Umno, MCA and MIC had shown this principle since independence.
“If they could do it back then, why can’t we do the same today?” he asked.
He urged leaders to sit down and settle any outstanding issues now rather than wait, and to work together as one big family.
“If we truly want to win, we must do what it takes to win. When we step into the contest, we fight until we win,” he said.
BN had introduced the GST at a rate of 6 per cent on April 1, 2015, when Najib was both prime minister and finance minister.
It was zero-rated on June 1, 2018, and formally abolished on August 31 that year when Pakatan Harapan swept to federal power for the first time.
The SST replaced it on September 1, 2018.
Under SST, sales tax is charged at 10 per cent on most taxable goods and 5 per cent on selected goods, while service tax is 8 per cent on most taxable services and 6 per cent on selected ones.
This is not the first time Zahid has made a similar pledge on the consumption tax.
In December last year, Zahid said that BN would accept SST for the time being but would insist on GST’s return after the next general election.
In September, he said Umno wanted GST back at a more reasonable rate and rejected a hybrid system that combines it with SST.
In October, he said GST should be refined and reintroduced if it was assessed as the right step for the country.

Title: Plants growing in toilets that cost 50 sen to use? Johor MB Onn Hafiz loses patience with Larkin Sentral after surprise visit
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 22 — Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi reprimanded the management of Larkin Sentral over broken facilities, dirty toilets and years of neglected maintenance during a surprise inspection yesterday, Berita Harian reported today.
He arrived at 8.30am after complaints and criticism on social media kept growing, and confronted the management over broken seats and lifts, dirty toilets, non-working escalators and potholed roads.
“Do I even have to teach you that?” he reportedly told those responsible for maintaining the terminal, as he voiced his disappointment with the state of the facilities.
He was unhappy that the toilets were so neglected that saplings could grow in them, even though users are charged 50 sen to enter.
When traders were asked to lift their shop shutters fully, he was told they had been broken for years, which led him to ask why nothing had been done.
“Whatever needs to be repaired, repair it,” he said.
“Can’t you see it’s dirty? This is our dignity,” he said in Malay, referring to the terminal’s condition and its role as a gateway to Johor Bahru.
Onn Hafiz stressed that basic maintenance should not need repeated intervention.
Berita Harian also reported that during this surprise visit, members of the public at the terminal told the menteri besar that he should conduct more frequent spot-checks as repairs had been delayed for a long time.
Some complained that the upper floor was unsuitable for business, that the lifts broke down often and that repairs to the escalator were unfinished.
Taxi drivers also took the chance to raise the badly damaged and potholed road surface at the terminal.
Onn Hafiz also inspected clogged drains and asked how long the rubbish had been left there.
He then directed the Johor Public Transport Corporation and Larkin Sentral’s management to repair the damaged facilities quickly, upgrade the toilets, provide more benches at the pick-up and drop-off areas and install more portable air conditioners in the waiting areas.
The management was also told to improve the cleanliness of the food court, fix the damaged road surfaces and review the bus ticketing system, including the extra charges imposed separately on passengers, to ensure better transparency.
The inspection followed an open letter to Onn Hafiz on November 11 that highlighted dirty toilets, dim lighting, disorganised bus platforms and unsatisfactory maintenance.
This is not the first time Onn Hafiz made an unexpected check on Larkin Sentral.
In July 2024, he said the terminal, which handles about 18,000 users a day, needed upgrades as the state worked to lift it from a grade B to a grade A terminal under the Land Public Transport Agency’s rating system.
Johor set aside RM2.5 million for the terminal’s upgrade in its 2025 budget, and in October 2025 Onn Hafiz said the second phase of the facelift was expected to be completed by the end of that year, after digital ticketing kiosks were installed in the first phase.

Title: Bersatu already talking about life after Muhyiddin, says Azmin Ali
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Bersatu has begun discussing who will lead the party after president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, its secretary-general has confirmed.
Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali said the talks, which include the process of handing over Muhyiddin’s leadership, were being carried out in an orderly manner to keep the party’s struggle going, Berita Harian reported last night.
“I want to stress that Bersatu is the only party that has started discussions on the transition of top leadership,” he was quoted as saying.
He said he had not heard of any other party doing the same.
Azmin said Bersatu was being fair to Muhyiddin, who declared three years ago that he no longer wanted to contest in party elections.
He said Muhyiddin carried on as leader only because the grassroots pressed him to stay, which he described as the party’s wish.
Muhyiddin announced a succession plan at a party convention in Selayang in July 2024, which gave Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin the deputy president’s post uncontested on the understanding that he would one day replace him.
In July this year, Muhyiddin said that plan had failed, causing divisions that forced the party to take disciplinary action against several members, and that his current term as president would be his last.
At Bersatu’s annual general assembly in September 2025, delegates approved a motion for Muhyiddin to remain president.
They also approved naming the Pagoh MP as Perikatan Nasional’s prime minister candidate for GE16.
Azmin said some Bersatu members who were earlier suspended or had turned their backs on the party had begun to return.
He said Bersatu was ready to welcome them for the sake of strengthening the party and serving the people.
“We are not severing ties with them,” he told Berita Harian, adding that the party had taken legal action in accordance with the Constitution.
“We may all have our mistakes and weaknesses, but if someone is prepared to apologise or do their best, we accept,” he added.
Bersatu had earlier suspended several leaders, including Beluran MP Datuk Seri Ronald Kiandee, a former party vice-president, and Masjid Tanah MP Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin, both linked to open support for Hamzah.
On May 8, the party suspended seven elected representatives for two election terms: Tanah Merah MP Datuk Seri Ikmal Hisham Abdul Aziz, Rompin MP Datuk Abdul Khalib Abdullah, Lumut MP Nordin Ahmad Ismail, Hulu Terengganu MP Datuk Rosol Wahid, Ketereh MP Datuk Khlir Mohd Nor, Kuala Sepetang assemblyman Ahmad Man and Chenderoh assemblyman Syed Lukman Hakim Syed Mohd Zain.
Three days later, it suspended two more leaders for two election terms: Mersing MP Muhammad Islahuddin Abas and Bukit Bunga assemblyman and Jeli division chief Mohd Almidi Jaafar.
